[h1]《slyders》简评 [/h1] [h3] 游戏背景及简评 [/h3] 本作故事设定在一个充满漂浮岛屿的世界，每个岛屿都有自己的居民和文化。然而，现在一个邪恶的霸主带着他的恶魔军队攻击了这个曾经和平的领域，并正在传播混乱和腐败。主角也就我们玩家将扮演一名狐狸战士，来挑战恶魔军队。游戏是一款经典的3d肉鸽射击游戏。 [h3] 优点 [/h3] 本作作为一款3d肉鸽类幸存者游戏，其优点相当突出。爽感方面做的十分出色，前期就就开始无双割草模式，战斗节奏紧张短促，爽感叠加十分显著。武器库方面数量众多，被动主动技能数种，也有像是召唤盟友例如大象的被动技能，十分有趣。此外场地不时掉落一些超强神器可以拾取并短暂使用，其威力更是无与伦比。此外游戏的配音方面相当出彩，打怪时的音效表现让作为割草以及肉鸽游戏爱好者的我沉沦。游戏的战斗手感极佳，作为一款射击类的肉鸽射击游戏来说相当出彩。游戏的画风明亮颜色鲜艳，武器以及特效方面光污染十足，十分炫酷，这对于一款肉鸽类射击游戏来说是非常大的加分点。 [h3] 缺点或可以改进之处 [/h3] 游戏没有自动射击选项，需要一直长按鼠标，过久了有点累。此外游戏的本地化问题比较严重，经常出现“口口口”字符，有点影响观感以及对游戏的理解。另外可以考虑一下伤害数字的大小，离远了就看不清了。还有游戏时不时出现bug，比如角色打着打着整个人变模糊然后进入无敌状态，升级后才会回归原样。另外可以考虑增加更多的初始武器，增加一些近战武器等等。以后希望能加入多人模式，这样玩起来会更爽快舒适。 [h3] 加分点 [/h3] 题材相当出彩，爽感方面出色，音效动感，光效亮眼，武器库丰富。实打实的一款精品3d肉鸽类幸存者射击游戏。 [h3] 总结 [/h3] 《slyders》作为一款3d肉鸽类幸存者射击游戏，在游戏核心“爽”与“刷”方面做得相当出彩与出色，喜欢肉鸽或者是射击游戏爱好者可以无脑入，虽然游戏目前存在一些本地化以及bug，不过制作组的更新较为频繁，可放心入等待改善。 闲暇时光：[quote] 闲暇时光，不妨试试游戏。 欢迎关注[url=store.steampowered.com/curator/45653622/] 闲暇時光鉴赏组 [/url] [/quote]

[h3] 7/10 [/h3] 爽游，但感觉像在EA阶段 ，虽然游戏很爽但是不能无脑爽，在酣畅淋漓的射击间隙要考虑走位，所以对身法操作有一定要求。 [h3] 游戏机制 [/h3] 游戏机制就是射爆，用枪杀掉面前的所有敌人，游戏自带4个主动技能槽和4个被动技能槽，还有冲刺键来脱身，主动技能要绑定键位主动释放，默认键位是右键、Q、1、2。被动技能会自己释放，主动和被动技能选择后会一直存在，直到玩家通关或死亡。地图有敌人上限，所以需要快速杀敌，否则敌人会进入狂怒阶段 主动技能包括： 1、召唤一束激光射向面前的敌人，与武器瞄准线一致 2、放置一座自动射击的炮塔 3、召唤空袭，包括一束从天而降的激光（类似绝地潜兵轨道炮？）和召唤一排炮弹对面前的一条竖线范围内敌人进行打击（需要在技能树解锁） 4、冲进敌阵一通砍杀，类似LOL剑圣的阿尔法突袭。 等等... 被动技能包括： 1、召唤一架无人机向敌人射击 2、场上出现NPC帮玩家杀敌，有大象和沙虫 3、每隔X秒自动向前发射一枚寻敌火箭，落点随机 4、每隔X秒放出一把在敌人之间弹射的手里剑 5、以自身为圆心，每隔X秒释放一道冲击波杀敌 等等... 游戏目前有四张地图，每个地图分为三类难度，依次解锁，每局15分钟，通关后会结算金币和宝石。游戏分为最后的大BOSS和中途的几个小BOSS，每隔一段时间还会刷新宝箱怪，宝箱怪类似暗黑破坏神的哥布林，会躲避玩家攻击，玩家在限定时间内击杀会获得金币和宝石。击杀小BOSS后会出现一个宝箱，近战攻击打开后会随机爆带词条的防具。 [h3] 武器 [/h3] 游戏内武器分两种，一是基础武器，除去初始的小手枪，游戏还额外有六把武器可解锁，解锁方式是通关地图后用金币解锁，包括初始的小手枪、射速快但威力低的汤姆逊，高威力低射速的霰弹枪等等。 另一种是杀敌获得的临时武器，包括霰弹枪、火箭筒、转管机枪，拾取掉落的BUFF后即可在有限时间内使用这些武器，威力比基础武器大。 [h3] 符文与技能树 [/h3] 符文基本就是游戏内杀敌获得的道具，只不过装配上对应的符文后会让你在一开始就解锁相应道具，有三个符文槽盒15个符文，也是用结算时获得的金币解锁。符文可以用宝石升级。 技能树用金币和宝石解锁，升级武器弹药、换弹速度、暴击率等在这里，宝石用来解锁强力（真强力吗？）技能可供在游戏中选用。 [h3]BUFF [/h3] 游戏内杀敌会掉落BUFF，有一个BUFF有点像逆战僵尸猎场的“极速狂热”天赋，一段时间内射速增加+无限子弹，BUFF可以叠加，如果捡到了火箭筒，又同时捡到了武器双持和射速增加，那就是毁天灭地的表现。 [h3]缺点 [/h3] 感觉游戏像没做完一样，虽然目前没解锁完全部地图但感觉已经把机制玩的七七八八了，后面就是一眼望到头的重复的刷。还有就是游戏“放冷枪”比较严重，弹幕游戏我躲不过去是我技术菜，但是在我身后放冷枪是真的难绷，尤其是低血量屏幕周边会泛红，更是难以察觉射过来的子弹，建议优化一下敌人子弹显眼程度或者降低身后敌人放冷枪的频率，在高难度下应付面前180°的敌人已经很难了还要时刻转身有点手忙脚乱，需要像DOOM一样不停的移动和观察四周。 还有，为什么没有自动射击，一直按着鼠标是有些累的。 [h3]总评 [/h3] 游戏只有第一人称，对晕3D人士和FPS新手有些不太友好，对玩多了FPS的老炮儿则不算什么问题。算的上是一款比较不错的FPS割草肉鸽，既喜欢割草又喜欢FPS又喜欢肉鸽的玩家不要错过，入就完事了。

[h1]Serious Furry-Sam[/h1] Slyders is a typical arena shooter in the style of Serious Sam, but its developers clearly decided to raise the bar and make everything not just brutally serious, but downright crazy. The main fox character must rip off demons, ED-209-like robots, chainsaw-wielding crabs, flying stingrays, and other evil creatures ready to tear him to shreds. Each enemy drops experience for leveling up, as well as a whole bunch of bonuses, be it temporary buffs or powerful weapons. Depending on the perks chosen, the fox himself can not only throw grenades and cause some explosions, but also call in an massive airstrike and unleash a elemental Armageddon. But don't think that's all there is to it. Why kill enemies alone when you can summon a charming little drone, a gladiator elephant, or a cute, giant graboid to your aid? Slyders doesn't dwell on emotions, the meaning of life, or any other such plot wastes, but instead throws you right into dynamic, adrenaline-pumping battles that will hook you from the very beginning and make you forget about time in an endless stream of reckless fun.

Despite some graphical bugs, this game felt like it had a lot of potential. Unfortunately, the dev has admitted to using AI generated assets, so I cannot support or recommend a game on ethical grounds. If I could I would refund the game, and strongly recommend people find other games that don't use AI. For those confused as to why this is an issue, the short of it is this: generative AI, like all LLM based AIs, requires huge amounts of whats called training data to "learn" how to do stuff. Due to the massive amounts needed, this data is stolen by scraping the internet, and/or through other shady data collection methods, often against the expressed wishes of artists or other creators. There are many other environmental, legal, and social issues with AI tech as well, but that's beyond the scope of a steam review :p Bottom line is that LLM AIs as they exist now are a fundamentally unethical technology, and so is its use. Its sad that even indie game devs have so little integrity or respect for artists these days, but I guess this is a learning lesson for me to start doing much more research into games before buying.

Slyders is an energetic and unapologetically chaotic first-person action game that blends elements of arena shooters, roguelite progression, and bullet-hell design into a compact but intense survival experience. Developed and published by Kato Games, the game immediately distinguishes itself through its bizarre yet charming premise, casting players as a fox warrior riding atop a high-speed, weaponized turtle in a floating fantasy world under demonic siege. This unusual setup sets the tone for everything that follows: fast, strange, and fully committed to excess. Rather than focusing heavily on story delivery, the game uses its narrative more as a flavoring, giving just enough context to justify the constant onslaught of enemies while keeping the player firmly centered on moment-to-moment action. At its core, Slyders is built around short, self-contained runs that typically last around fifteen minutes, making it well suited for repeat play sessions. Each run drops the player into wide, open arenas where enemies spawn continuously, surrounding you from every direction with melee attackers, ranged units, and projectile-spamming threats. Combat is relentless, demanding constant movement and spatial awareness as the screen fills with bullets, explosions, and visual effects. Unlike traditional shooters that emphasize cover or precision pacing, Slyders thrives on aggression and mobility, encouraging players to stay in motion, circle enemy packs, and make snap decisions under pressure. The bullet-hell influence is especially apparent when projectile patterns overlap and force you to weave through narrow gaps while still maintaining offensive momentum. Progression during a run is rapid and frequent, forming the backbone of the game’s addictive loop. Enemies drop experience that allows you to level up at a brisk pace, often multiple times within a single minute, and each level presents a selection of random upgrades. These upgrades can dramatically reshape your playstyle, offering stat boosts, new weapons, passive effects, or powerful active abilities. Some runs may emphasize raw firepower, while others lean into area control, summoned allies, or screen-clearing abilities. This randomness gives each session a distinct rhythm and encourages experimentation, as players chase powerful synergies that can turn overwhelming chaos into controlled devastation. Between runs, longer-term unlocks and meta-progression add a sense of continuity, slowly expanding your arsenal and making future attempts feel more flexible without completely removing the challenge. Visually, Slyders embraces clarity through simplicity, favoring clean, readable environments designed to support high-speed combat rather than detailed exploration. Arenas are large and functional, allowing players to kite enemies and reposition as threats escalate, while distinct environmental themes help prevent visual monotony. Character models, effects, and enemy designs lean toward stylized exaggeration, which helps maintain readability even when the screen is saturated with action. Performance is generally solid, with the game handling large enemy counts and dense projectile effects without severe slowdowns, though visual clutter can occasionally make it difficult to track individual threats. This is an expected trade-off in a game that pushes spectacle as hard as Slyders does. The sound design supports the gameplay effectively, prioritizing feedback over flair. Weapon sounds, enemy cues, and ability activations provide useful audio information during intense moments, helping players react even when visual information becomes overwhelming. The music maintains a high-energy tone that complements the frantic pacing, though it tends to fade into the background over longer sessions. While not especially memorable on its own, the soundtrack serves its purpose by sustaining momentum without distracting from gameplay, reinforcing the idea that Slyders is primarily about mechanical engagement rather than atmospheric immersion. That said, Slyders is not without its rough edges. Balance can feel uneven, with certain upgrade combinations leading to overwhelming power while others struggle to keep pace with later enemy waves. Difficulty spikes can be abrupt, especially for new players still learning enemy behaviors and optimal movement patterns. Quality-of-life features and customization options are relatively minimal, which may frustrate players looking for deeper control over visuals or input settings. These shortcomings do not undermine the core experience, but they do highlight areas where refinement could significantly improve accessibility and long-term comfort. Taken as a whole, Slyders is a confident indie shooter that knows exactly what it wants to be: fast, chaotic, and endlessly replayable in short bursts. It may not appeal to players seeking deep narrative arcs or methodical pacing, but for those who enjoy high-pressure survival gameplay, rapid build experimentation, and the sheer thrill of turning overwhelming odds into explosive victory, it offers a compelling and distinctive experience. Kato Games’ willingness to embrace absurdity and mechanical excess gives Slyders a strong identity, making it stand out in the growing crowd of roguelite shooters as a game that thrives on momentum, experimentation, and controlled chaos. Rating: 8/10

小品级的肉鸽割草FPS，4个地图3难度全通大约5个小时。 体验上就是放弃思考，升级也不太需要考虑搭配，毕竟也没有构筑，左键不松就完事了。 简单的玩法循环，局外有着【天赋】【技能】【装备强化】【武器解锁】这4个养成项目，然后在关卡中获得装备与货币。 关卡中就是幸存者机制，击杀敌人获得经验，然后4选1强化，同时同一种强化项目有着不同等级之分。 每个关卡15分钟，但是单调的体验15分钟一局玩起来有些累，感觉10分钟的一局即可。 4个场景大同小异，找块平坦的地方割草就行，除非想被植物或者石头卡住挨打，或者被起伏的土丘挡住弹道。 装备系统就是简单粗暴的加属性，不同级别的装备仅仅是加的值不同，并没有能与局内强化相互搭配进行构筑，毕竟局内的 升级强化也只是加属性。这是最平庸的肉鸽了。（万金油搭配，穿加经验的装备就行） 而且当我解锁了从roll的天赋后，发现基本上没什么用，升级选项就那些选什么基本上都能用，无非是早点选和晚点选的区别。 在难度平衡上，墓地地图难度感觉是要比最后一关的雪地难度要高，甚至如果dps不足，法师会无限召唤全小怪最快的直线移动速度的眼球怪，很容易被耗死。同时怪的花样也丰富。 就5-6把武器里还有完全的上位替代。 爽完所有关卡和难度后，解锁了最后的技能，虽然我也不会再浪费时间再开一把去体验了。

This is a rogue-lite arena boomer shooter. I would say that this is in the top three for me in this genre. Gameplay is fast, smooth, and chaotic. The graphics are good, adding the spectacle of lasers, explosions, and giant Dune worms as you fight. Guns are satisfying to shoot, with a nice punch to them. The buffs you get throughout a mission allow you to strategize and try new things on new runs. It's just a very well crafted game. I will say it take a little while for the progression to get going. I was on the fence for the first hour or so, but once it gets going, and you discover where the progression is, it becomes a really satisfying game. Give it the 2-hour try. Busy Dad approves.

Slyders actually caught my attention once I saw it on one of those Steam Nextfests. I tried the demo and fell in love with it, because it's actually fun to shoot and survive monsters in this game, even more with the mix of Vampire Survivors in it, where each level you get upgrades and skills to make the killing and surviving better. Of course, I bought it when it was possible. I would say this game is a bit asset flippy, because a number of models from the game are third party, like the main character, the mobs, and also including the bear character that flies around Aryx, which I saw in another game as a npc (I don't remember the game name). Also counting that the developer made use of Generative AI to make some graphics of the game, like the skill icons, because, at least from what they said, some artist refused to work with them to sketch them. There are currently 4 areas in the game, each with 3 difficulties. The areas are different from each other, with each area having different themes, monsters, bosses and also music. The thing I don't really like, is how early in the stage the mob spawn is so lacking, but it increases as the time passes. Also speaking of the music, the stages music is actually pretty badass. They surely stimulate shooting a lot of monsters for all those precious exp and golds. The most disappointing region so far is the ice region, which, no pun intended, is very anti climatic. The music and enemies rooster, aswell as the map itself, I don't like it. Without counting that the final bosses from the 3rd and 4th worlds can be cheesed if you get far away from the boss. As you play the game, you can get enough golds or crystals to buy new weapons, unlock new perks or even more stuff to improve your run. You can even unlock relics or something that allow you to start a new run with certain weapons maxed out. But you need to pick carefuly which one you'll use, since you can only have 3 active at the same time. I think that the worst so far in the game, is that the latest update nerfed the difficulty to the point that anyone can survive even the hardest difficulty of the stages without many issues. Beside the guns function way better now, the mobs no longer feel that threatening anymore. At least doesn't need to make such rigid build making, like I was doing of stacking Restoration on every run just for the passive health regen. I do actually recommend playing this game if you want a game just to shoot some stuff, while listening to badass music. Also, for some reason the fox character doesn't have a tail. But I guess would be better to complain at who made the model, heh. Edit: Also, Brian is pretty useless.
